kit.name: ELEGOO UNO R3 Most Complete Starter Kit

identity.canonical_name: MAX7219-driven 8x8 LED dot matrix display module
identity.manufacturer: The display driver chip (MAX7219) was originally made by Maxim Integrated, now part of Analog Devices. The assembled module itself is generic and unbranded.
identity.manufacturer_part_number: MAX7219 (the driver chip). The underlying 8x8 LED matrix part is commonly a 1088AS or 1088BS red common-cathode matrix on modules like this one, but that exact part number was not confirmed for ELEGOO's specific board by a source I fetched.
generic_equivalents: any MAX7219-based 8x8 LED matrix breakout module
identity.package: assembled module: a small PCB, about 32mm square, with an 8x8 grid of LEDs mounted on top of a MAX7219 driver chip, plus two 5-pin headers (an input side and an output side) for chaining several modules together

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A small grid of 64 tiny lights, 8 rows by 8 columns, that can show simple pictures, numbers, or scrolling text, all controlled with just 3 wires from the Arduino.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Simple pixel displays: scrolling text, small icons, animations, or a basic level meter.
function.how_it_works_briefly: The MAX7219 chip built into the module does all the fast row-by-row switching needed to individually light up 64 LEDs. The Arduino only has to send it a stream of on/off, brightness commands one bit at a time (a method called serial communication) over 3 control wires, and the chip handles turning the right LEDs on and off many times per second.

pinout.name: DIN
pinout.notes: serial data from the Arduino; ELEGOO's tutorial wires this to Arduino pin 12

pinout.name: CS
pinout.notes: ELEGOO's tutorial wires this to Arduino pin 11

pinout.name: CLK
pinout.notes: ELEGOO's tutorial wires this to Arduino pin 10

pinout.name: VCC
pinout.notes: output side header, passes power on to the next module in a chain

pinout.name: DOUT
pinout.notes: feeds the DIN pin of the next module when chaining several matrices together

pins.pin_1_identification: The module has two 5-pin headers on opposite edges, both silkscreened with their pin names. The header whose data pin is labeled DIN (not DOUT) is the input side, the one you wire to the Arduino first (components101 module datasheet).

electrical.operating_voltage: DC 4.7V to 5.3V, typical 5V (ELEGOO's own tutorial); a third-party module datasheet gives a slightly wider 3.7V to 5.3V for the same style of module
electrical.absolute_max_voltage: not confirmed from a source I fetched
electrical.typical_current: not separately confirmed; ELEGOO's tutorial lists only an 'Operating Current' figure of 320mA
electrical.max_current: 2A (ELEGOO's own tutorial states a 'Max Operating Current' of 2A, which reflects the worst case of all 64 LEDs lit at full brightness)
electrical.logic_level: not confirmed from a source I fetched; since the module runs from a 5V supply, its logic signals are almost certainly 5V level

key_specs.daisy_chainable: yes, several modules can be wired output-to-input to make a bigger display using the same 3 control wires
key_specs.pcb_dimensions_mm: about 32 x 32, per the components101 module datasheet; ELEGOO's exact board dimensions were not separately confirmed
key_specs.arduino_library_used: Maxmatrix, per ELEGOO's own Lesson 15; other published tutorials for the same hardware commonly use the LedControl or MD_MAX72xx library instead

visual_identification.shape_and_size: Small square PCB, about 3.2cm on a side, with a grid of 64 LEDs mounted on top and a black rectangular driver chip soldered to the board
visual_identification.color_and_markings: Typically a red 8x8 LED grid (the color most commonly shipped in this kit); the driver chip is usually printed with 'MAX7219'; two 5-pin headers on opposite edges, commonly labeled with the pin names or marked IN and OUT
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: Look for 'MAX7219' printed on the black driver chip, and the pin names VCC, GND, DIN or DOUT, CS, CLK silkscreened near each header
easily_confused_with: A bare, unassembled 8x8 LED dot matrix display with no driver chip and no header, which needs external shift registers or a separately wired MAX7219 chip to work
a MAX7219 7-segment display module, which uses the same driver chip but a different kind of display

wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: Maxmatrix library (ELEGOO's Lesson 15); LedControl or MD_MAX72xx are common alternatives used by other tutorials for this same hardware

hazards: None significant; low voltage display module
handling_notes: Do not exceed the module's 5.3V maximum supply
Handle the board by its edges to avoid flexing the solder joints under the LED grid
common_mistakes: Wiring the Arduino to the OUT-side header instead of the IN-side header, which stops the module from responding
Uploading code written for a different library (Maxmatrix versus LedControl versus MD_MAX72xx) without installing the matching one first

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: Power or DIN/CS/CLK wiring mismatch, or the wrong library installed
symptoms_and_causes.check: Recheck wiring against ELEGOO's Lesson 15 diagram, confirm 5V and GND are connected, and confirm the correct library is installed

symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: The 5V supply cannot provide enough current, or brightness is set too low in software
symptoms_and_causes.check: Confirm the 5V source can supply up to 2A at full brightness (ELEGOO's own spec) and check the brightness setting in the code

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With the module powered from 5V, measure DC voltage between the VCC and GND pins on the input header; it should read close to 5V. The serial data lines (DIN, CS, CLK) are fast pulsing signals, so a multimeter cannot show them meaningfully; use the Arduino sketch's visible output on the display itself as the real test.

typical_suppliers: Amazon (often sold in packs of 3 to 5)

confidence.notes: Important correction to the seed record: this item does not ship as a bare 8x8 LED matrix driven by two separate 74HC595 shift registers as the seed guessed. Both ELEGOO's current kit parts list and its own tutorial (Lesson 15) confirm it ships as a single pre-assembled module that combines the 8x8 matrix with an onboard MAX7219 driver chip, wired with only 3 control signals (DIN, CS, CLK) plus power. This module is confirmed present in the current EL-KIT-001 kit.
